teaser.text: CK Asset Holdings Limited is a property-led group that earns money from homes, rents, hotels, services, pubs, utilities and investments. The useful question is not just what it owns, but how a customer’s payment becomes revenue, meets costs and reaches the group.

stock.title: CK Asset stock forecast
stock.meta_description: CK Asset stock forecast: scenario prices, key drivers, cash generation and today’s valuation.
stock.opening: CK Asset’s weighted share price is HK$44.62 in October 2027 and HK$48.66 in October 2029. It hinges on CK Asset turning asset backing and disposal proceeds into repeatable earnings.
stock.closing: The full memo also explains CK Asset’s business, rivals, management and risks.

blocks.heading: Where could CK Asset’s shares go?

paragraphs.text: The weighted price is HK$44.62 in October 2027. That implies a 4% return. It is HK$48.66 in October 2029. That implies a 21% return. The bear case probability is 30%. The base case probability is 55%. The bull case probability is 15%.

The probability-weighted share price is HK$44.62 in October 2027, for a 4% return from today’s HK$44.50 including dividends. It reaches HK$46.24 in October 2028, for a 12% return. By October 2029, the weighted price is HK$48.66, for a 21% return. The three-year range runs from HK$22.84 in the bear case to HK$78.11 in the bull case.

blocks.heading: What has to go right or wrong for CK Asset?

paragraphs.text: Second-half 2026 launches of Victoria Blossom in Kai Tak and further units at The Greenwich Phase 2 in Beijing will test whether sales replenish profit as well as cash. FY2026 and following annual results will show how scheduled sales convert, how the loss of the UK businesses affects earnings, and where disposal cash goes. Stronger project margins, better office leasing, productive reinvestment or shareholder returns support the bull case; weak margins, impairments or lower returns on retained cash support the bear case. Remember: the discount earns its keep only when asset backing becomes repeatable earnings.

blocks.heading: How much cash does CK Asset really make?

paragraphs.text: Operating cash flow was HK$18,670 million in 2025. A HK$9,049 million release from properties for sale supplied a large part of that strength. This is normal development timing: land and construction absorb cash for years, then handovers release inventory and customer money. It does not prove that the next projects will earn the same return.

blocks.heading: What does an investor pay for CK Asset?

paragraphs.text: At HK$44.50, CK Asset has an equity market value of HK$155,740.14 million. Its 0.4x price-to-book ratio means investors pay roughly forty cents for each dollar of accounting equity. Its 11.4x forward P/E means the price equals 11.4 times forecast profit, while the 4.0% dividend yield describes the current cash distribution, not a promised return.

dividend.title: CK Asset dividend: history, coverage and yield
dividend.meta_description: CK Asset dividend history, cash coverage, forecast changes and today's yield, explained in plain English.
dividend.opening: CK Asset paid HK$1.74 per share in 2024, with the base forecast rising from HK$1.78 to HK$1.86 by October 2029. Operating cash flow was HK$18,670 million in 2025, although HK$9,049 million came from releasing properties for sale, so dividend coverage was helped by development timing.
dividend.closing: The full memo also explains CK Asset’s business, rivals, management choices and risks.

blocks.heading: How much does CK Asset pay per share?

paragraphs.text: Base dividends rise from HK$1.78 per share to HK$1.86 by October 2029. The bear case cuts them to HK$1.50, while the bull case lifts them to HK$2.15. The base reflects the small recovery from HK$1.74 in 2024 and the absence of a special dividend. Thin development contribution, at HK$765 million on HK$21,618 million of sales in the first half of 2026, limits confidence in faster growth. Dividend odds are 50% base, 30% bear and 20% bull.

blocks.heading: Is CK Asset’s dividend covered by its cash?

paragraphs.text: From 2021 to 2025, dividends and buybacks absorbed a large share of the company’s capital returns, with buybacks concentrated in 2021 and later repurchases diminishing. By 2025, buybacks had stopped, while cash dividends had also fallen from their earlier level. These payments follow payment dates, so they are not necessarily the dividends declared for the same financial year.

Operating cash flow was HK$18,670 million in 2025. A HK$9,049 million release from properties for sale supplied a large part of that strength. This is normal development timing: land and construction absorb cash for years, then handovers release inventory and customer money. It does not prove that the next projects will earn the same return.
